Featured projects

FactoryMind — Predictive Maintenance

Machine-failure prediction with a FastAPI backend, a RAG maintenance assistant, and a Streamlit dashboard

Factories lose money when machines fail unexpectedly, but real failures are rare, so a model can look accurate while missing almost all of them. I built a failure-prediction system on the AI4I 2020 synthetic dataset (10,000 machine-operation records, only 3.39% of them failures). It starts with a configurable sensor-data validation layer (missing values, numeric conversion, range constraints, non-finite values), followed by a Logistic Regression pipeline with standardized features and stratified train/validation/test splits.

The baseline scored 96.85% accuracy but caught only 13.24% of failures, which is why I evaluate on recall and precision rather than accuracy. Tuning the decision threshold lifted validation recall to 43.14% at 42.31% precision (F1 0.4272), and the next steps target better recall still.

GlowBot — Skincare Assistant with Memory Fabric

LeMiCi IQ · full-stack
A chatbot that remembers each user across conversations, built on a company-initiated memory architecture

Most chatbots either forget everything between sessions or resend the whole chat history with every message. GlowBot sorts what users tell it before the model replies. A rule-based memory router sends each message to short-term memory (Redis) or long-term episodic and semantic memory (PostgreSQL), ChromaDB holds pointers for retrieval, and a verified skincare catalog (FAISS) keeps product recommendations grounded. I contributed to the memory fabric and built the chatbot and web app around it.

The app is a React (Vite) chat interface on a FastAPI backend with LangGraph orchestration, async replies, saved chat history, typing indicators, and a “GlowBot Remembers” profile that shows what it has stored about the user. Docker containerization and cloud deployment are in progress.

Sign Language Interpreter — v2

final year project · upgrade
Landmark-based recognition with a desktop GUI, built as the direct upgrade of v1

v2 rebuilt the same problem from a different angle: instead of detecting bounding boxes per frame (heavier, and capped at the six gestures it was trained on), it uses MediaPipe to extract 21 hand-landmark coordinates per frame, normalizes them for position invariance, and classifies the resulting feature vector with a Random Forest model — chosen over CNNs and SVMs for its balance of accuracy, speed, and small-dataset efficiency. The vocabulary grew to the full alphabet, digits 0–9, and space (37 classes, 3,700 images), and the whole thing runs inside a PyQt5 desktop app with a live gesture overlay, a running sentence buffer, and clear/reset/save controls — turning single-letter predictions into readable words in real time.

Sign Language Interpreter — v1

6th sem · minor project
Detection-based gesture recognition, presented at ICEAT 2024, Hyderabad

Hearing loss affects roughly 430 million people worldwide, and interpreters aren't always accessible or affordable. This project set out to translate hand gestures into text in real time, using nothing but a webcam — no wearables, no depth sensors. A four-person team built a custom dataset for six core gestures (Hello, I Love You, No, Yes, Thank You, Please), hand-annotated it in LabelImg, and trained a YOLOv5 object-detection model to recognize gestures directly as bounding boxes in the video feed.
